title: Checkpoint: A Changed Empire
objective: After this level you can explain how the empire of 395 differed from the empire of Augustus.
summary: By 395 CE the empire was Christian, ruled by distant monarchs, split in two and defended partly by Goths under their own leaders.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 finale. Would Augustus have recognized the empire of 395?
cards.body: Line up the empire of 395 CE against the one Augustus left. Four big changes made it a different world.

cards.headline: A different empire
cards.body: By 395 CE the empire was Christian. It was divided into East and West, with two capitals: Rome, and Constantinople, dedicated in 330 CE. After Theodosius died in 395 CE, his two sons divided it between them. And it was defended partly by Germanic allies under their own leaders, like the Goths who settled inside the empire after Adrianople. Three changes down.

cards.headline: Lord, not first citizen
cards.body: The fourth change was the emperor himself. Augustus had called himself princeps, “first citizen,” and avoided the title of king. Later emperors dropped the modesty and ruled openly as absolute monarchs, surrounded by elaborate court ceremony. Historians sometimes call this the Dominate, from dominus, “lord.” From first citizen to lord: Augustus might not recognize the job.
cards.callout: Dominate: rule by a lord, not a first citizen

cards.headline: Chapter 9 complete
learned: By 395 CE the empire was Christian
It was divided into East and West
Goths served as allies inside it

questions.prompt: What happened to the empire after Theodosius died in 395 CE?

options.label: It was reunited under one emperor
It was divided between his two sons
It returned to the old gods
It became a republic again

questions.explanation: Theodosius was the last to rule both halves; his sons divided it.

questions.prompt: How did the emperor’s image change from Augustus to the late empire?

options.label: From king to elected consul
options.rationale: The change went the other way.

options.label: From “first citizen” to open monarch
From general to priest of Vesta
From monarch to first citizen
options.rationale: The change went the other way.

questions.explanation: Augustus posed as princeps; later emperors ruled openly as lords, dominus.

questions.prompt: Why did the empire of 395 need two capitals?

options.label: It was divided into East and West
Rome had been destroyed
The Senate refused to leave Rome
Christians banned the old capital

questions.explanation: East and West each had its own emperor and its own capital.

questions.prompt: Chapter 9 recap: which change after Adrianople put the empire at risk?

options.label: Goths were banned from entering the empire
Christians took control of the whole army
Goths settled inside under their own leaders
Rome stopped minting the silver denarius

questions.explanation: After 378 CE, Gothic groups settled inside the empire under their own leaders, a new and risky arrangement.
